_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoking: Counting last week and planning the next...

description: Use this when a plan from plan_lanes has ended and the user says what got done, such as "here is my list with what I ticked, plan next week". Input tips: send checklist, the todo_text with [x] on finished lines, pasted whole; it carries the lanes and the hours. Without the text, send lanes as the earlier answer returned them (build required), done and not_done task titles or ids, and hours_per_week. One of checklist or lanes is required. Optional: start_date, days, days_off, next_steps for the build lane, swap_in to move a parked interest into the open slot, keep_hours. Returns the done count per lane, the changes it made (carried build steps, a paused side quest when build stalled, fewer hours after a week under 40%), and the next plan in the same shape as plan_lanes, with new todo_text. Tie-break with plan_lanes: every review of a plan that is in this chat comes here. Not for a first plan (use plan_lanes), a calendar booking or a diagnosis.

checklist.description: The main input: the todo_text from plan_lanes or review_week with each finished line ticked as [x], sent whole from its first line "Lane plan: ...", up to 8000 characters. Its header lines carry the lanes, the hours and the parking lot, so nothing else is needed. Send checklist or lanes; one of them is required.

days.description: How many days to plan, 3 to 7. Defaults to the length of the pasted plan, else 7.

days_off.description: Weekdays with no tasks, such as ["Sun"]. Defaults to the days off in the pasted plan.

done.description: Finished tasks, up to 60: titles as written, such as "Build: Indie iOS app: set up the Xcode project", or ids such as "d1-1". Needed with lanes; with checklist the [x] marks are enough.

hours_per_week.description: Hours for the next plan, 1 to 80, such as 10. Defaults to the hours in the pasted text; needed with lanes.

keep_hours.description: Keep hours_per_week even when less than 40% got done. By default the next plan uses 20% fewer hours then.

lanes.description: Only when no checklist is sent: the lanes object plan_lanes or review_week returned, build required, such as {"build": {"name": "Indie iOS app"}, "open": {"name": "Guitar"}}. Send done, not_done and hours_per_week with it.

build.description: The build lane as last returned, such as {"name": "Indie iOS app"}.

open.description: The open lane as last returned, or null when it was empty.

reading.description: The reading lane as last returned, or null when it was empty.

next_steps.description: New next steps for the build lane, such as ["add notifications"]; they come after the carried ones.

not_done.description: Unfinished tasks, up to 60: titles or ids, such as "d3-1".

spine.description: The user's own one-sentence direction that ties the interests together. Leave it out to get a first guess.

start_date.description: First day of the plan as YYYY-MM-DD, such as "2026-10-08". Use today in the user's time zone, even mid-week; do not move it to a Monday or to tomorrow unless the user asked to start then. Defaults to today in UTC.

swap_in.description: Name of a parked interest the user wants in the open slot now, such as "Guitar"; the current side quest is parked with a bookmark.

name: review_week

budget.description: Minutes per lane over the whole plan; build, reading, open and review add up to total_minutes.

open.description: Minutes for the side quest; 0 when it is empty or paused.

reading.description: Minutes for the reading lane; 0 when it is empty.

review.description: Minutes for the review task on the last work day.

total_minutes.description: All planned minutes: the weekly hours scaled to the days of the plan.

changes.description: Plain sentences on what the review changed for the next plan: carried build steps, a paused side quest, fewer hours, a swap from the parking lot. Tell them to the user.

days.description: The plan day by day, from start_date.

items.description: The tasks of the day in order; empty on a day off.

id.description: Task id, d<day>-<n>, such as "d2-1" for the first task of day 2. review_week accepts it in done or not_done.

tag.description: The lane of the task, or review for the weekly review task on the last work day. A carried build step keeps tag build and its title ends with " (carried)".

title.description: Task title that starts with its lane, such as "Build: Indie iOS app: set up the Xcode project".

minutes.description: Sum of the task minutes on this day.

off.description: True on a day off; it has no tasks.

lanes.description: Each interest in its lane. Send this object back as review_week.lanes to review the week without the text.

build.description: The build lane; there is always one.

minutes.description: Minutes this lane gets over the whole plan.

name.description: Interest name, as the user gave it.

note.description: The user's note on it; empty when none was given.

time.description: The same minutes in words, such as "6 h" or "1 h 30 min", or "none this plan" when minutes is 0. Repeat it as is.

why.description: One sentence on why this interest has this lane.

open.description: The open lane, or null when no interest fills it.

minutes.description: Minutes this lane gets over the whole plan.

name.description: Interest name, as the user gave it.

note.description: The user's note on it; empty when none was given.

time.description: The same minutes in words, such as "6 h" or "1 h 30 min", or "none this plan" when minutes is 0. Repeat it as is.

why.description: One sentence on why this interest has this lane.

parking_lot.description: Interests that wait this plan, each with a bookmark; nothing is dropped.

bookmark.description: Where to pick it up next time.

reading.description: The reading lane, or null when no interest fills it.

minutes.description: Minutes this lane gets over the whole plan.

name.description: Interest name, as the user gave it.

note.description: The user's note on it; empty when none was given.

time.description: The same minutes in words, such as "6 h" or "1 h 30 min", or "none this plan" when minutes is 0. Repeat it as is.

why.description: One sentence on why this interest has this lane.

next_step.description: What to tell or ask the user next.

notes.description: Short sentences on choices the tool made, such as a guessed spine or an interest moved to the parking lot. Often empty.

review.description: The count of last week's tasks. The review task itself is not counted.

by_lane.description: The same count per lane; a lane with no tasks last week is left out.

not_done.description: Tasks not done in this lane.

done.description: Tasks ticked or named as done.

done_percent.description: done as a share of all tasks, 0 to 100. Under 40 means fewer hours next plan unless keep_hours is true.

spine.description: The one sentence that points the lanes at the same direction.

sentence.description: The spine sentence. Ask the user whether it fits.

source.description: given: the user's own words from spine. derived: a first guess from the lanes.

status.description: Always ok; a call that cannot plan returns an error instead.

todo_text.description: The plan as paste-ready text: header lines (Lane plan, Spine, the lanes, Parking lot), then one "- [ ] title (minutes) #id" line per task. Give it word for word; review_week reads it back.

title: Review a week and re-plan
